choices.text: Write only for your own worlds

effects.log: Your worlds alone know.
Making should be discovered.

events.text: A prayer rises from a maker below who has heard of a god of talisman: they ask for one sign that their work matters.

effects.log: Their work glows once. They never stop making.

choices.text: Send a dream of a better method

effects.log: They wake knowing more.
You let it pass.

events.text: A temple whose priests have grown old asks you for a clay attendant before the next world is born, and lets it be known that a god who shapes servants for the pantheons would take less faith.

choices.text: Take it, at a fair offering

effects.log: You make it. The client returns.

choices.text: Take it, at the rival's price

effects.log: You make it for less. They are pleased.
You decline. Gods value what is refused.

events.text: You need clay from the first riverbank, and there is little of it left in the sky this age. A god of Fortune offers you some, at a price.

effects.log: You pay. The work goes on.

choices.text: Go to where it is found

ok.log: You go to the edge of the sky and bring back enough.

effects.log: You wait. Gods can.

events.text: A work goes wrong in front of other gods: the clay crumbles back into riverbank. Three pantheons hear of it.

effects.log: You laugh. Gods remember the laugh.
You study it for an age and understand.
You blame them. Fortune is offended.

events.text: A god born an age ago asks to learn puppetry at your hands and the first riverbank's clay, and has never made anything but trouble.

effects.log: You teach them. In an age they make a world's weather.

ok.log: They pass.

choices.text: Send them to a god who shapes servants for the pantheons

effects.log: You send them on. The rival is surprised.

events.text: A god who shapes servants for the pantheons challenges you before the Heavenly Court: one work each, judged by an elder god who dislikes both of you.

ok.log: Your work is chosen. Gods talk of it for an age.

effects.log: You make one together. It is the best work in the sky.
You decline. The rival tells three pantheons.

events.text: Your method of puppetry appears in a lesser god's work, done wrong. A world below is suffering for the mistake.

effects.log: You mend the world first, then find the god.

choices.text: Take it to the Heavenly Court

effects.log: The Court fines the god.
You teach them properly. They are ashamed and grateful.

events.text: You have what you need to attempt an attendant that prays. It may take an age. Gods have broken themselves on such work.

ok.log: It works. The pantheons speak of it until the end of the sky.

fail.log: It fails at the end, as such works do.

effects.log: You wait, and grow.
You make a lesser work, perfectly.

events.text: A temple whose priests have grown old wants a clay attendant that bends a law of the world a little in their favour, and offers a pantheon's friendship for it.

effects.log: You make it. The friendship comes. Somewhere a world bends.
You make it true. They use it, displeased.
You refuse. The pantheon is cool to you.

events.text: A mortal below who prays to makers has carved a tiny copy of a clay attendant, badly, and left it on your altar.

effects.log: You bless their hands. Their village has the best carvings in its world.
You keep it on your bench, always.

events.text: The Feast of Domains asks every maker of puppetry in the sky to bring one work to its table.

effects.log: Your work is admired by three pantheons.
You bring theirs. They shine.
You watch, and learn.

events.text: A pantheon will not accept a clay attendant from a god who stands in no pantheon, however fine it is.

choices.text: Make it for a small world instead

effects.log: You give it to a small world. They worship it.

ok.log: They take it, and resent needing it.

choices.text: Seek a pantheon's name for it

effects.log: A pantheon lends its name for a share.

events.text: A sleeping god dreams of where clay from the first riverbank is hidden, and the dream leaks into yours.

ok.log: You find it at the dream's end.

fail.log: The dream ends before you arrive.

effects.log: You tell them when they wake. They give you half.

events.text: A quiet age at your hands and the first riverbank's clay. No wars, no commissions. Only clay from the first riverbank and the slow gold sky.

effects.log: You make something no god will see. It is your best.
You give them to small worlds.
You rest.

events.text: A god brings back a clay attendant you made an age ago, broken in a war. They want it mended, because it saved their life.

choices.text: Mend it so the break shows

effects.log: You mend it with light in the crack. They are moved.
You make it new. It is not the same.
You refuse. Some things should stay broken.

events.text: Gods at the Star Market argue whether your puppetry is Perfect-Grade. Fortune herself is listening.

ok.log: Perfect-Grade, says Fortune. Your works are sought across the sky.

effects.log: Arguments sell.

events.text: A god of the Unlit Sun wants a clay attendant and will not say why. They pay in dark faith.

effects.log: You make it. You never learn what for.
You refuse. They leave quietly.

choices.text: Make it so it fails if misused

ok.log: You make it so. It fails at the right moment.

events.text: The god who first made a clay attendant, at the first dawn, comes to your workshop and watches you without a word.

effects.log: You keep working. They leave a mark on your bench. Your work is better forever.
They show you once. It takes an age to understand.
They take it, and smile.

events.text: A god who shapes servants for the pantheons offers a secret of puppetry for one of yours, sworn on the Book of Fates.

effects.log: You trade. Both of you are greater.
You lie on the Book. It remembers.
You refuse.

events.text: A pantheon at war wants a hundred of a clay attendant for its host, by the next age.

effects.log: You make them. The war is shorter. Or longer.
You make half and say so.
You refuse. The pantheon is cold.

events.text: A mistake in a clay attendant makes something no god has seen before.

effects.log: You keep it and make it a method.
You unmake it. Some new things are dangerous.

events.text: A world below is dying of something puppetry could cure, and it has no god of makers to pray to.

effects.log: You make it and send it down. The world lives, and does not know whom to thank.

choices.text: Teach a mortal there to make it

effects.log: You teach a mortal in a dream. It takes longer. It lasts.
You leave it. You will hear its silence for an age.

events.text: A god you love faces a war for their domain. You could make a clay attendant for them, the best you have ever made.

effects.log: You make it with everything you have. They carry it and win.

choices.text: Buy the best from a god who shapes servants for the pantheons

effects.log: You buy it. It is very good. It is not yours.

events.text: A teacher of a divine college watches you work puppetry for an age, and asks if you would teach the young gods.

effects.log: You teach. Some of them will make worlds.
One lesson, spoken of for an age.
You decline.

events.text: A pilgrim at your temple breaks a clay attendant kept on the altar, and kneels, terrified of what a god will do.

effects.log: You lift them up and tell them it was only a thing.

choices.text: Make them a small one to take home

effects.log: You give them one. Their world worships makers now.

events.text: Your hands and the first riverbank's clay is worn by an age of work. A new one would be better. It would not remember your hands.

effects.log: You make a new one. It learns you, slowly.
You keep it. Your work is slower and truer.

choices.text: Give it to a young god

effects.log: You give it on. They treat it as holy.

events.text: False a clay attendant from the Market Beyond the Twelve floods the Divine Exchange, and the worlds cannot tell the difference.

effects.log: You ask less faith.

ok.log: Your sign cannot be forged. Gods seek it.

effects.log: They are small gods, starving. You give them true work.

events.text: The head of a pantheon asks for an attendant that prays, and says only that it is for the end of a war.

ok.log: You make it. The war ends.

fail.log: It falls short. The war goes on.

choices.text: Ask which side it ends the war for

effects.log: They tell you. You decide.

events.text: A god who shapes servants for the pantheons is fading, their worshippers dying out below, with a great work unfinished.

effects.log: You finish it in their name. Their worshippers return.
You take it.
You send them worlds. They live to finish it.

events.text: You could write puppetry into the Book of Fates itself, so every world born after knows a little of it.

effects.log: You write it. New worlds are born knowing how to make.

choices.text: Write only for your own worlds

effects.log: Your worlds alone know.
Making should be discovered.

events.text: A prayer rises from a maker below who has heard of a god of puppetry: they ask for one sign that their work matters.

effects.log: Their work glows once. They never stop making.

choices.text: Send a dream of a better method

effects.log: They wake knowing more.
You let it pass.

events.text: You learn that above the clouds a pill can be tuned to the qi method of the one who takes it. A pill for a fire method tastes of ash to everyone else.

choices.text: Tune one to your own method

effects.log: You brew one for yourself. It is like drinking your own voice.
You sell tuned pills. The Lotus Halls take notice.

events.text: Your cauldron floats a hand above the bench on its own heat, as all cauldrons do above the clouds, and today it drifts out of the window.

ok.log: You catch it on a bridge, pill still cooking.

fail.log: It lands in a lake of cloud. You fish it out a week later.

effects.log: It comes back at dusk, like a cat.

events.text: An immortal facing their next tribulation in a month asks you for a pill to survive it. There is no such pill. They know it. They ask anyway.

choices.text: Make them a pill for courage

effects.log: You make one for courage. It does nothing. They survive.
You tell them. They thank you, and train harder.

events.text: The Lotus Halls offer you a seat among their alchemists, if you will brew only for them.

effects.log: You accept. Your pills go to the cracked and the dying.
You refuse. Your cauldron answers to you.

events.text: A peach of the three-thousand-year trees fell into your cauldron by accident, and the pill that came out smells of spring.

effects.log: You eat it. For a year you are very happy and very slightly younger.
You sell it to a minister for a ridiculous price.

events.text: Starsteel must be folded under the light of a falling star, and the next one falls tonight, over an isle half a day's flight away.

ok.log: You fold three blades under its light.

fail.log: You arrive as the light fades.

effects.log: You wait a decade. It falls on your roof.

events.text: A convoy captain brings a blade they have carried for a thousand years and asks you to rework it with starsteel without changing what it is.

ok.log: It comes back stronger and still theirs.

fail.log: It comes back stronger and not quite theirs.

choices.text: Tell them to keep it as it is

effects.log: You tell them it is already perfect for them. They leave happy.

events.text: A blade brought to your forge for reworking whispers, and what it whispers is the name of the immortal it last killed.

choices.text: Rework the whisper out of it

ok.log: It goes quiet. Its owner weeps with relief.

fail.log: The whisper moves into your anvil.

effects.log: You refuse it. Some blades are better left as they are.

events.text: A forge of the Star Forge falls through a crack in its isle into the sea of cloud, and its master asks to share your anvil.

effects.log: You share it. Two masters at one anvil argue and make wonders.
You refuse. They find another anvil.

events.text: A blade you made a century ago has earned a name of its own in the duels of the isles. Its owner asks you what you meant to call it.

effects.log: You tell them the name you whispered at the quench. They use it.

choices.text: Say the blade chose its own

effects.log: They like that better.

events.text: You lay an array over a whole isle road for the first time, and feel every footstep on the road for three days.

effects.log: You learn the road better than its wardens.
You soften it until you can sleep.

events.text: An immortal asks you to lay an array that hides their pavilion from the Jade Court's eyes.

ok.log: The pavilion disappears. You never ask why.

fail.log: The Court sees the array anyway.

effects.log: You refuse. Hiding from the Court is not your trade.

events.text: A storm is coming that will break the moorings of a small isle, and its elders ask you for a ward before dawn.

ok.log: The ward holds. The isle keeps its moorings.

effects.log: You lay a simple one. It is enough.

events.text: Under your pavilion you find an array older than the Jade Court, still running, holding something down.

effects.log: You leave it. You sleep a little worse.

ok.log: It holds down a fallen immortal's anger. You strengthen it.

events.text: You find that ten Low stones laid in the right array become one Mid stone, better than the Exchange gives. The Exchange will not like this.

effects.log: You do it quietly for a century.
You teach it. The Exchange changes its rate.

events.text: You stand in the Thunder Gate, where tribulations are let through into the Upper Realm, and let a small one go through you.

ok.log: Your body comes out harder than starsteel.

fail.log: You come out singed and wiser.

effects.log: You step out. It was enough to know.

events.text: A duellist of the isles asks to temper beside you, and spends the first day watching you suffer with an expression of great respect.

effects.log: You teach them. They thank you in a duel a century later.
You prefer to suffer alone.

events.text: Sky-iron sand fell in a storm on the next isle, and the isle's children are playing in it. It will strip their skin if they are not careful.

choices.text: Gather it before they are hurt

effects.log: You gather it. The children are disappointed. Their parents are not.

choices.text: Teach them to temper with it

effects.log: You teach them a game that is tempering. They will be strong.

events.text: There is a waterfall of cloud at the edge of the Upper Realm that falls forever into nothing. Old immortals temper under it.

effects.log: You sit under it. It is very cold and very quiet.
You look. There is nothing. You come back changed.

events.text: An immortal who tempered in the Thunder Gate for a thousand years tells you that a body is never finished, only stopped.

effects.log: You keep going. They nod.
They say they have not. They are smiling.

events.text: You write your first conditional talisman: it will do nothing until someone lies in its presence. You hang it in your doorway.

effects.log: It flares once a month. You learn a great deal about your visitors.
You sell it to the wardens.

events.text: A skiff captain wants a talisman that wakes only when a storm comes out of nowhere, which above the clouds they always do.

effects.log: You write it. The captain never loses a skiff again.

choices.text: Write ten and sell them on the moorings

effects.log: They sell out by noon.

events.text: A talisman you wrote a century ago and forgot, whose condition was a name spoken, flares in a stranger's hand at the Exchange.

ok.log: It was the name of someone you loved below. The stranger is their grandchild.

effects.log: You let it be. Some conditions are kept without you.

events.text: Cinnabar ground from a fallen star is so bright it burns the paper unless you write in the dark.

effects.log: You write by feel. The talisman is perfect.
You dilute it. It is safer and weaker.

events.text: The Jade Court wants talismans to seal its archive against fire, and asks the best writers of the isles.

effects.log: Your seals are chosen. The archive is safe.

choices.text: Write them, and one more for yourself

effects.log: You keep one copy of the Court's seal. Just in case.

events.text: Puppets strung with cloud-silk move like weather, which is beautiful and very hard to control.

effects.log: It obeys, mostly. It also dances when you are sad.
You use plain thread. The puppet is obedient and dull.

events.text: A house of the Eight wants a puppet door-warden that will let in only those the house likes, and remember everyone it refuses.

ok.log: It works. It refuses an heir of the house once, and is right to.

fail.log: It refuses everyone, including the house.

effects.log: You build one that only remembers.

events.text: You build a puppet porter for a Lantern Guild house, and it carries stones better than any hired hand. The hired hands come to complain.

effects.log: You build each of them a puppet to work beside them.
They are not comforted.

events.text: A puppet you left on your bench overnight has moved. Not far. It is facing the window.

effects.log: You leave it. Some mornings it faces you.
You unstring it. You are almost sure it was only the wind.

events.text: A troupe of the drifting isles asks you to build puppets for a play about the first immortal to climb the white stairs.

effects.log: You build them. The play runs for a thousand years.

choices.text: Build them, and play a part

effects.log: You work one of the puppets yourself, every night for a season.

events.text: A Dao pill is a law of the world pressed small. The first one you make holds the rule that water runs downhill, and it is very heavy.

effects.log: You take it. For an age, you understand slopes.

choices.text: Give it to a world that floods

effects.log: You give it to a world that floods. Its rivers learn.

events.text: A god of a lesser river is fading because their river has been dammed below. They ask you for a pill to live without it.

ok.log: They live, thin and grateful.

effects.log: You send a flood below. The dam breaks. The god lives.

events.text: The Harvest asks you to distil the first nectar of a new world, which will set how sweet its fruit is forever.

effects.log: Its fruit will be sweet forever.
Its fruit will be bitter and its people strong.

events.text: The War Domain wants a pill that lets a god fight on after their domain is lost.

effects.log: You make it. Wars last longer now.
You refuse. The War Domain remembers.

events.text: A mortal alchemist below prays to you every night before the cauldron. Their pills are terrible.

choices.text: Send them a dream of the right method

effects.log: Their pills are good now. Their village lives longer.

choices.text: Let them learn on their own

effects.log: They learn, slowly.

events.text: The oldest gods of the Green Assembly ask you to brew for their council, which has not taken a new alchemist in three ages.

effects.log: You accept. Your pills are grown, not made, now.
You decline. They respect it.

events.text: In a ruined temple you find a recipe for a pill no god remembers, written in a language only the dead speak.

ok.log: You learn it and brew the pill. It restores a lost memory to whoever takes it.

fail.log: The recipe will not be read.

effects.log: You leave it for whoever comes next.

events.text: Fortune asks you for a pill that makes luck, and offers you a share of what it makes.

effects.log: You make it. Somewhere, someone loses the luck it made.
You make one that shares it out. Fortune is intrigued.

events.text: The first fire of your cauldron goes out, the fire lit at the first dawn, which no god has relit.

choices.text: Relight it from your own domain

effects.log: You relight it with a piece of yourself. It burns warmer.
Hwarin gives fire, and remembers.

events.text: You work a piece of your own domain into a blade for the first time. It is like cutting your own hair, and then like cutting your own hand.

effects.log: You finish it. Part of you is in that blade forever.
You stop. The blade is half divine and half nothing.

events.text: Metal from a dead sun is so cold it burns. A god of War wants a spear of it.

ok.log: The spear is the coldest thing in the sky.

fail.log: It burns your hands through to light.

effects.log: You make a shield. The god of War is disappointed and alive.

events.text: A god of the Sea wants a blade with a sea inside it, so that every cut is a tide.

ok.log: You forge it. Every cut is a tide.

choices.text: Forge it with a lake instead

effects.log: A lake is calmer. The god is not impressed.

events.text: In the War Domain's armoury you find a hammer from the first war, cracked. Its god asks you to mend it, and to never ask what it broke.

effects.log: You mend it and do not ask.
You ask. You wish you had not.

events.text: The smiths of Hwarin's Hearth invite you to strike one blow on their great anvil, an honour given once an age.

ok.log: Your blow rings through the sky.

fail.log: Your blow is a little off. They are kind about it.

choices.text: Ask a smith to strike for you

effects.log: They strike. You learn by watching.

events.text: A mortal smith below prays for a blade that will save their village from raiders. They pray every night with their hammer in their hand.

choices.text: Guide their hammer in a dream

effects.log: They forge the best blade of their life. The village stands.
A blade appears on their anvil. They are afraid of it.

events.text: An artefact you made an age ago has rebelled against its god, and refuses to be wielded. The god blames you.

ok.log: It listens to its maker. It goes back.

effects.log: You remake it. It forgets its rebellion.

events.text: Two gods want rings forged from their two domains, so that they cannot break their vow to each other.

effects.log: You forge them. Their domains are bound.
You warn them that such rings cannot be undone. They forge them anyway.

events.text: The anvil that rang at the first dawn rings again on its own, once, in your workshop.

effects.log: You strike it. It answers. You understand metal now.
You let it ring. It is enough to hear it.

events.text: You design your own sign, a pattern of the sky that is yours alone, to be laid in every array you make from now on.

effects.log: Your sign is simple and strong.
Your sign is beautiful and gods remember it.

events.text: A pantheon asks you to lay an array over a whole region of the sky, so its enemies cannot cross it.

ok.log: The region is closed. The pantheon is safe.

fail.log: The array tears at one edge.

choices.text: Lay a weaker one that lets the innocent through

effects.log: You lay a kinder one.

events.text: An array of yours tore, and a region of the sky went dark. Small worlds there are frightened.

ok.log: You mend it. The sky brightens.

effects.log: You hang lanterns of faith until it is mended.

events.text: Cutting a godstone along the lines of a domain, you find another domain inside it, very small, with a god in it the size of a grain.

effects.log: You set them free. They grow, slowly.
You keep it. The small god sleeps on.

events.text: A pantheon at war asks for an array that will collapse an enemy's domain into itself.

effects.log: You lay it. A domain collapses. Its worlds go dark.
You refuse. The pantheon is cold.

events.text: An array-god of the Silent Hall shows you an array made of silence, and asks if you can see it.

ok.log: You see it. They are impressed.

effects.log: They laugh. That was the right answer.

events.text: A mortal below has drawn a crude array in the dirt that, by accident, is calling to you.

effects.log: You answer. The mortal falls on their face.

choices.text: Fix their array so it calls a kinder god

effects.log: You fix it. A kinder god answers.

events.text: Laying arrays across the sky for an age, you realise you have drawn a map of the whole Divine Realm that no other god has.

effects.log: You keep it. It is worth a pantheon.

choices.text: Give it to the Heavenly Court

effects.log: The Court is grateful and wary.

events.text: A young god has wandered into an array you laid and cannot find the way out.

effects.log: You lead them out. They want to learn arrays now.

choices.text: Teach them to find the way

effects.log: You teach them from outside. It takes an age. They find it.

events.text: Hwarin's Hearth takes a body as a smith takes iron. You step into the fire for the first time.

ok.log: You come out unbending.

fail.log: You come out smaller, and wiser.

effects.log: You step out. The fire remembers you.

events.text: A god's body is partly their domain. When a world in your domain suffers, you feel it in your bones.

effects.log: You temper it into strength.
You go and ease it.

events.text: A god who walked out of the Hearth unburned challenges you to sit in it as long as they did.

ok.log: You sit as long. They bow.

effects.log: You decline. They grin.

events.text: A young god of War asks you to make them hard enough to never lose a war.

effects.log: You temper them. They lose anyway, and live.

choices.text: Tell them that is not what bodies are for

effects.log: They do not understand. Yet.

events.text: A star falls and you stand under it, as the oldest gods once did.

ok.log: It breaks on you. You do not break.

effects.log: You step aside. The star makes a crater you name.

events.text: A mortal below prays to grow strong enough to carry their family through a famine.

effects.log: They carry their family through.
Food is better than strength.

events.text: After an age of tempering, your body asks for rest in a voice you have never heard it use.

effects.log: You rest an age.
You ignore it. It does not ask again.

events.text: An old god who tempered in the first storms tells you a body is a promise to the world, not a weapon.

effects.log: They say you will find out.
You bow. They pat your shoulder.

events.text: An heir of the Elder Lineages says a god of no old house can never temper truly, and offers to prove it.

ok.log: You outlast them. The Lineage is quiet.

effects.log: You laugh. They do not know what to do.

events.text: You write a talisman of Dao law for the first time, and the law it carries is that a promise must be kept.

effects.log: Promises made there are kept.

choices.text: Give it to a world that lies

effects.log: The world learns to keep its word.

events.text: Your new brush is made from a god's old name, given freely when they took a new one. It writes in their old voice.

effects.log: Your talismans carry their old strength.
You give it back. They weep, and take it.

events.text: A god whose borders keep moving asks for a seal that will hold them still for an age.

ok.log: The borders hold. The god sleeps.

choices.text: Write one that moves them back gently

effects.log: You write a gentler one.

events.text: A scribe of the Hall of Fate says your talismans of law are crossing out lines in the Book.

effects.log: You stop. The Book is calm.
They tell you. The lines were cruel.

events.text: A world below has no law against killing its own gods. You could write one.

effects.log: You write it. Its gods sleep better.
You write the larger law. It is harder to hold.

events.text: Two pantheons hang talismans of law on their borders that contradict each other, and the sky between them shudders.

choices.text: Write a third that reconciles them

ok.log: The sky is still.

effects.log: You strengthen one. The other falls.

events.text: A mortal below writes your name on paper and hangs it over a cradle, believing it a charm.

effects.log: You make it one. The child is never ill.
It is only paper, and love, which is often enough.

events.text: You write a talisman so true that the Dao itself pauses to read it.

effects.log: The Dao reads it and nods. You are spoken of in three pantheons.

choices.text: Burn it before it is read

effects.log: You burn it. Some things should not be finished.

events.text: Your ink, a law of the world, has run out. Making more means taking a law from somewhere it is needed.

choices.text: Take one from a dead world

effects.log: A dead world does not need its laws.

choices.text: Wait for a new law to be born

effects.log: You wait an age.

events.text: Clay from the first riverbank remembers the hands that first shaped it. Your first attendant moves like someone you never met.

effects.log: It serves your temple, and sometimes hums.
It points at the sky. You do not ask again.

events.text: An attendant you shaped for an old temple has begun to pray, on its own, at dawn.

effects.log: It prays every dawn. The temple fills.
You unshape it gently. Some things are too strange.

events.text: A temple whose priests have grown old asks for clay attendants to keep its rites when the last priest dies.

effects.log: You shape them. The rites go on.

choices.text: Teach a mortal to keep them instead

effects.log: You send a young priest a dream.

events.text: A god who shapes servants for the pantheons says your attendants are too kind to be useful.

effects.log: You make them kinder. The small temples want them.
You make them obedient. The pantheons buy them.

events.text: A pantheon at war asks for a host of clay soldiers.

effects.log: You shape them. They fight and crumble, and the gods go home.
You refuse. Clay should not be made to die.

events.text: The first riverbank is running out of clay, and every maker of the sky wants what is left.

effects.log: You take your share.

choices.text: Leave yours for the young makers

effects.log: You leave yours. They remember.

events.text: An attendant asks, in a clay voice, whether it may stop serving.

effects.log: You free it. It walks off to see the sky.
It says it wants to make something. You give it clay.

events.text: A child below has made a clay doll and prayed for it to move.

effects.log: It moves once. The child never forgets.

choices.text: Let the child grow up to do it

effects.log: The child becomes a great maker.

events.text: Shaping a new attendant, you find your hands making the face of someone from your life below.

effects.log: You finish it, and keep it in your study.
You smooth it away. Not yet.

events.text: Word runs along every road: a pill of nine colours has fallen out of the sky into a valley, still warm. Houses and wanderers are racing to it, and an immortal has come down the white stairs to claim it. Something in you knows the hand that made it.

ok.log: You reach it first. It knows you, somehow, and goes quiet in your hands.

fail.log: You come second. You were close enough to touch it.

choices.text: Let the strong fight over it

effects.log: You watch from the ridge. Whoever takes it, it was made by someone like you.

events.text: A light falls through the Divine Realm's floor into the sea of cloud: a cauldron made by a god now faded, a Divine Work. The factions are already flying. You feel, very faintly, that you have held it before.

ok.log: You reach it in the mist. It settles in your hands as if it had been waiting.

effects.log: You let them fight. It will find its way, as such things do.
